chunks: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
"They only considered the marking of the sacrificial camels (ishʿār) good because with the first drop that falls from its blood, Allah forgives him for that."

key_terms.إِشْعَارَ: the marking of the sacrificial animal, especially the camel, as designated for sacrifice
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who grants forgiveness and reward
key_terms.الْبُدْنِ: the sacrificial camels offered in hajj
key_terms.دَمِهَا: its blood, meaning the blood of the sacrificial animal
key_terms.قَطْرَةٍ: a single drop, here referring to the first drop of blood
key_terms.يَغْفِرُ: forgives; Allah grants pardon and remission of sin

ai.seo_question: Why was ishʿār of sacrificial animals considered a meritorious act in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the virtue behind ishʿār, the marking of sacrificial camels in hajj. It indicates that this act was regarded favorably because Allah grants forgiveness from the very first drop of the animal’s blood.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "The practice of marking the sacrificial animal (Ish’ar) was deemed good because at the very first drop of its blood that falls, Allah (swt) forgives the person for that act."
